ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, UK HM Treasury Consolidated Sanctions List (extending to Gibraltar), EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (for continuity and correspondent-bank expectations), OFAC SDN and Non-SDN Lists (mandatory as best practice for any USD-denominated wire or Wise settlement), and all Gibraltar Sanctions Notices issued under the Sanctions Act 2019. PEP identification is required with enhanced due diligence (EDD) for any PEP, family member, or close associate match; adverse-media and source-of-wealth verification is mandatory for beneficial owners holding 25% or more; screening must be refreshed at minimum every 90 days and upon any material change in ownership.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies Registry, administered by the Civil Status and Registration Office (CSRO), Government of Gibraltar — electronic name availability search and reservation via the official e-Services portal at https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory language is English. Corporate names must be expressed in Latin (Roman) script; Greek, Cyrillic, Arabic or other scripts are not accepted for registered legal names, and transliteration into phonetic English is mandatory for any non-Latin source name. The suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd' is mandatory for a company limited by shares or guarantee. A name will be rejected if it is identical or deceptively similar to a name already registered or reserved on the Gibraltar register.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Limited / Ltd (restricted to companies limited by shares or guarantee only)
Bank / Banker / Banking (requires Gibraltarian banking licence and GFSC ministerial consent)
Insurance / Assurance / Reinsurance / Insurer (requires GFSC authorization)
Trust / Trust Company / Trustee (requires licensed trust service provider status)
Royal / Crown / King's / Queen's / Majesty (implies royal or governmental patronage; requires ministerial consent)
Government / Minister / Ministry / Authority / Agency (implies official sponsorship; prohibited unless authorized)
University / College / Institute / Academy / Chamber of Commerce (requires sector regulator approval)
Building Society / Investment Fund / Pension Fund (regulated tokens requiring financial-services authorization)
Gibraltar / Rock / British / UK (geographical tokens that may mislead as to government connection; require supporting consent)
Group / Holdings / International (requires a demonstrable group or cross-border commercial rationale)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may: (1) electronically re-file with a revised name after a mandatory 48-hour cooling-off period without additional fee; (2) file a formal administrative appeal with the Registrar of Companies within 21 calendar days of the rejection notice, submitting a statutory declaration of entitlement and, where relevant, the notarized written consent of the objecting rights-holder; (3) if the Registrar affirms the rejection, apply for judicial review before the Supreme Court of Gibraltar under the Civil Procedure Rules (Gibraltar) Part 54 within three months of the affirmation; (4) a licensed Gibraltar corporate service provider or local counsel may lodge and manage the appeal on behalf of the applicant; extension of a reserved name may be granted for a further 30 days upon payment of the prescribed extension fee, subject to the Registrar's discretion for bona fide incorporation pipeline delays.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole registered office. The Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar) requires a physical registered office located in Gibraltar and capable of receiving service of process. A virtual mailbox or co-working address may supplement but may not replace this requirement; the registered office must be occupied and managed by a licensed corporate service provider (TCSP) for the exempted-company structure, and the Gibraltar address must appear on all commercial correspondence and the statutory register.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 0.65 quantified probability (65%) of unannounced on-site inspection within the first 24 months, elevated because the business scope is AEO/customs supply-chain auditing, which attracts cross-border HMRC/Gibraltar Customs information-sharing and GFSC physical-substance verification for licensed TCSP premises.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 2014 of Gibraltar (Cap. 100 as consolidated), Part II (Incorporation and Company Names), ss. 3-38, and Part IV (Registers and Officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Gibraltar Companies House, Registrar of Companies, 72 Melinda Street, Gibraltar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form A (Application for Registration of a Company) together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies; a single fully paid Ordinary Share of GBP 1 issued to the founding subscriber is customary for a non-resident exempted company; no escrow, bank deposit, or capital blocking requirement is imposed at incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company in Gibraltar, as notified to the Registrar, is adopted. RESOLVED that the subscriptions set forth in the subscribers' return are accepted, and the directors are authorized to allot and issue Ordinary Shares at par to the founding subscribers upon full payment. RESOLVED that the persons named in the certificate of incorporation be appointed as directors and that the person named as Secretary be appointed Company Secretary, each to hold office until the second annual general meeting. RESOLVED that the directors be and are hereby authorized to file the incorporation documents, to register the Company as a non-resident exempted company, to open corporate bank accounts, and to do all acts necessary for the AEO supply-chain consulting business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House, Company Names Reservation Desk (online via Companies House e-Services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed corporate name ending in Limited or Ltd through the online name reservation portal, together with the prescribed reservation fee. Provide a certified extract of the subscribers' resolution authorising the chosen name, and verify that the name does not conflict with existing names or contravene the restricted-name provisions of s. 42 of the Companies Act 2014.
required_dossiers: Name Reservation Request form
Certified resolution authorising the name
Subscribers' passport copies for identity verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or sensitivity, file a written representation distinguishing the name from any cited prior mark, or submit up to three alternative names for immediate re-screening.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution, and Notarisation of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Gibraltarian Notary Public acting with corporate legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association in conformity with the Companies Act 2014, determine the share capital and subscriber allotments, insert the first directors and secretary provisions, and arrange for subscribers to execute the documents in the presence of a Notary Public for authentication of signatures.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Association
Articles of Association
Executed subscriber signature pages
Notarised identity documents of all subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar's model template is required, restate the constitutional documents using the prescribed statutory form and re-execute before the notary; any irregularity noted by counsel is cured by supplemental deed approved by all subscribers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing of Form A and Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House, Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form A (Application for Registration of a Company) through the Companies House e-filing portal with the notarised Memorandum and Articles, a Statement of Compliance, the approved registered office address, and signed consents of each director and the secretary, and pay the incorporation fee by BACS debit from the filer's Companies House account.
required_dossiers: Form A under s. 5 of the Companies Act 2014
Certified copy of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
Statement of Compliance signed by the subscribers
Officer consent forms for all directors and the secretary
Registered office address consent letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the Registrar's query letter by re-filing the corrected Form A or supplementary documentation within fourteen days; repeated queries may be resolved through a compliance meeting at Companies House or by written legal submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House, Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfaction of the registration conditions, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation by email and hard copy; verify the company number, legal name, and date of incorporation, and circulate the certificate to the subscribers and the appointed officers.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (government-issued)
Registered company number confirmation record
Proof of payment of the incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Apply under the Registrar's administrative correction procedure for rectification of any clerical error in the certificate, or request a certified duplicate re-issue if the original certificate is lost or damaged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Registered Office and Opening of Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House and the appointed Registered Office Provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Formally adopt the physical registered office address in Gibraltar as approved by the Registrar, file the address notification in the electronic companies register, open the register of members, register of directors, register of secretaries, and register of charges at the registered office, and enter the initial share allotments and officer details.
required_dossiers: Registered office adoption notification
Statutory registers opening record
Change of registered office notice if the address differs from Form A
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a compliance inspection finds the registered office ineffective, file the change-of-registered-office form without delay and obtain the new provider's signed consent, with the effective date antedated to the date of the board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Gibraltar Non-Resident Exempted Status Registration and Tax Assurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office (Commissioner of Income Tax) with the Gibraltar Ministry for Digital and Financial Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for recognition as a non-resident exempted company, submitting the certificate of incorporation, the register of members, declarations of beneficial ownership, and audited or accountant-certified particulars, and obtain the Commissioner's certificate of non-residence confirming zero-rate corporate income tax treatment outside Gibraltar taxable territory.
required_dossiers: Application for non-resident exempted company status
Certificate of Incorporation
Register of members and share allotment record
Beneficial ownership particulars under the Beneficial Ownership Act
Declaration by the directors that central management and control remain outside Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Appeal any refusal to the Tax Board of Appeal within thirty days, correcting beneficial ownership and control documentation, or resubmit the application with revised declarations confirming absence of local trading revenue.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Gibraltar Industrial Licensing Board, Department of Trade (informational only; no physical industrial licence is triggered for ISIC 7020 management consultancy services)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing permit is required for ISIC 7020 / NAICS 541614 supply-chain compliance auditing in Gibraltar; the AEO certification and security-audit service is delivered as an unlicensed professional consulting activity in line with the target business scope

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Gibraltar Department of Environment and Climate Change (DECC)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no EIA screening or registration required under the Environment Act 2021 for office-based professional consultancy with no physical development, construction, or manufacturing footprint
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A for industrial discharge; commercial waste handling must comply with the Waste (Gibraltar) Regulations, and office HVAC/IT emissions fall below the regulated VOC thresholds applicable to non-industrial premises

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service for the adopted registered office; structural load inspection for any dedicated server or archive suite; and workplace notification to the Gibraltar Occupational Safety and Health Authority under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2000

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar, Commissioner of Income Tax / Income Tax Office (ITO), Ministry of Finance; e-filing portal: https://etax.gibraltar.gov.gi. Indirect and customs matters: HM Customs Gibraltar, Gibraltar Customs House; portal: https://www.customs.gi.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Bermuda Exempted Company establishing a Gibraltar presence must: (1) file a certified copy of its Bermuda certificate of incorporation and constitutional documents with the Gibraltar Companies Registry (Companies House, under the Companies Act 2014) for registration as a Gibraltar External Company, appointing a Gibraltar-resident agent and registered office; (2) obtain a Gibraltar Tax Identification Number by filing a Corporate Registration Form (Form IT-1) with the Income Tax Office, disclosing directors, beneficial owners, registered office and expected Gibraltar activities; (3) if employees are engaged locally, register for PAYE with the ITO employer registry prior to first payroll; (4) if goods are imported/exported, obtain a Gibraltar EORI number (format: GI + 12 digits) from HM Customs Gibraltar, either directly or through a licensed customs broker or an Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) with streamlined procedures; (5) if operating through a fixed place of business in Gibraltar, register the establishment as a permanent establishment for corporate income tax and file annual returns at the 12.5% corporate rate. There is no minimum capital requirement, no prior tax clearance for incorporation, and no share-capital duty.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: The Bermuda Exempted Company qualifies as tax-exempt in Bermuda under the Exempted Companies Act 1981, provided an annual filing fee and government fee are paid and no undertaking in Bermuda is carried on beneficially by the company. This exemption applies only in Bermuda. In Gibraltar, the entity is treated as a foreign company and is subject to entity-level taxation at 12.5% on profits attributable to a Gibraltar permanent establishment, and on Gibraltar-source income arising directly or indirectly; no territorial remittance exemption applies to the Gibraltar branch. There is no pass-through or look-through treatment for Gibraltarian tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar has no check-the-box or entity-classification election mechanism. The Bermuda Exempted Company may elect in Bermuda to apply for a tax exemption certificate (valid to 2050) to bind Bermuda from future taxes. In Gibraltar, there are no hybrid or dual-residency election regimes; anti-hybrid and CFC rules operate under the Income Tax Act 2010 (as amended, implementing OECD BEPS and EU ATAD-aligned standards) and mandatory disclosure rules (DAC6-style) apply for reportable cross-border arrangements. A company may file a formal determination of residence claiming management-and-control outside Gibraltar to argue non-residence, but this is a factual determination by the ITO, not an elective regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None (no VAT, no GST, no general sales/use tax). Gibraltar was excluded from the EU VAT area and, post-Brexit, remains outside the UK VAT system. Limited indirect taxes are levied instead: customs import duties (Import Duties Act), excise duties on alcohol, tobacco, hydrocarbon oils and gambling equipment, environmental/vehicle import charges, and stamp duty on property/shares/documents. Supplies of services, including AEO certification consultancy, are outside the charge to any general indirect tax, regardless of place of supply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable: GIP 0 (nil) VAT/GST registration threshold because no VAT/GST regime exists in Gibraltar. However, any person importing goods into Gibraltar (including the exempted entity for its office equipment or client cargo under audit) must hold a Gibraltar EORI number and must register with HM Customs Gibraltar; there is no turnover threshold for customs registration. Import duty is chargeable on specified categories of goods (principally alcoholic beverages, tobacco, fuels, vehicles, and selected luxury items); the majority of goods, equipment and professional samples enter duty-free.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-connected e-invoicing obligation exists in Gibraltar; invoices for consultancy or audited supply chains may be issued in paper or PDF format. For movement of goods, all import and export declarations must be lodged electronically with HM Customs Gibraltar using the Gibraltar Electronic Customs Declaration system (internationally formatted SAD/ICS/AES messages) via approved software or a licensed customs broker; AEO-certified operators may use simplified declaration and self-assessment procedures with expedited clearance and reduced examination rates. There is no continuous transaction control (CTC) mandate linking invoice issuance to customs clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable: Gibraltar does not levy VAT/GST, so there is no 0% export VAT rating, no VAT registration, and no VAT refund mechanism for unavoidable input tax. Exported goods from Gibraltar to a third country (including the UK and the EU) are outside the scope of Gibraltar import/excise duty, and no duty relief claim is required. For supplies of AEO audit services performed in Gibraltar for overseas clients, no indirect tax is chargeable and no zero-rating documentation is needed. If the Bermuda Exempted Company were separately UK-VAT-registered for UK activities, UK standard VAT rules would apply to those UK activities only, and genuine export of goods from the UK could qualify for UK VAT zero-rating subject to UK proof-of-export rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Gibraltar Customs export declaration (electronic SAD/AES format) stamped with movement reference
Commercial invoice and detailed packing list
Bill of Lading (sea) / Air Waybill (air) / CMR consignment note (road) evidencing goods leaving Gibraltar
Inward remittance certificate (bank SWIFT MT103 or Wie/Wire transfer confirmation) evidencing payment from the overseas counterparty
Certificate of Origin (only where preferential tariff relief is claimed under UK–Gibraltar or UK–third-country trade agreements)
AEO Security and Safety Certificate (where the operator or the audited supply chain is certified, to evidence simplified compliance)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Although no VAT zero-rating fraud is possible in Gibraltar, false or incomplete customs declarations attract severe penalties under the Customs and Excise Duties Act and related regulations: civil fines up to GIP 10,000 or 100% of the duty evaded per declaration, seizure and forfeiture of goods, retrospective clawback of any duty relief or free-circulation treatment, and suspension or revocation of AEO certification. Criminal prosecution for fraudulent evasion, smuggling, or false statements can result in unlimited fines and imprisonment of up to 7 years. For income tax, deliberately inaccurate export documentation that distorts profits attributable to the Gibraltar permanent establishment exposes the entity to penalties up to 100% of the unpaid tax, interest, and potential loss of the Bermuda tax exemption certificate if the Bermuda authorities find linked misrepresentation. Export records and underlying documentation must be retained for at least 6 years from the date of the relevant transaction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Her Majesty's Government of Gibraltar through the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC); monetary policy and currency anchoring are provided by the Bank of England (GBP parity for the Gibraltar pound / GIP).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Gibraltar pound (GIP) is pegged at a 1:1 parity to pound sterling and is fully convertible for both current-account and capital transactions. There are no exchange-control approvals or profit-remittance permits; a Bermuda Exempted Company operating or maintaining banking relations in Gibraltar may freely convert and repatriate profits, subject only to standard AML/CFT source-of-funds verification and any applicable economic-substance documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Gibraltar imposes no statutory surrender or compulsory conversion of export receipts. A company may retain, convert, and disburse foreign-currency export proceeds in any eligible account without a mandated timeline; only suspicious-transaction reporting and sanctions screening obligations apply under the GFSC AML/CFT framework.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. Digital EMIs such as Wise can onboard a Bermuda Exempted Company for multicurrency deposits and low-value wire disbursements, but they are not licensed credit institutions in Gibraltar and cannot legally offer GIP clearing, corporate overdrafts, letters of credit, or high-value trade settlement. EMIs must be used only as a secondary disbursement rail for client refunds or low-risk operational payments, never as the primary treasury account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Gibraltar-licensed banks generally require at least one director or senior beneficial owner to complete a face-to-face due diligence interview inside Gibraltar or, in low-risk and well-referenced cases, a supervised interactive video call. Remote-only opening is not viable for a tax-exempt Bermuda Exempted Company; the bank also expects the original notarized and apostilled corporate pack to be lodged through a local professional intermediary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bearer shares or incomplete beneficial-ownership chain within the Bermuda Exempted Company structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Certificate of Incumbency, statutory register of members and directors, beneficial-ownership declaration signed under Gibraltar's Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018, notarized and apostilled copies, and an institutional reference from the company's current professional bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt status of the Bermuda Exempted Company flagged as potential tax-haven avoidance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bermuda Economic Substantiation Statement confirming economic substance in Bermuda, Gibraltar tax-residency certificate or proof of no taxable nexus, FATCA/CRS registration confirmation, substance narrative for the AEO supply-chain audit activity, and audited or certified financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk classification of customs and security auditing services in a supply-chain audit context
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid AEO certificate or pending-AEO application letter, detailed AEO security-audit contracts, internal AML/CFT policy, sanctions-screening results for counterparties, and documented upstream/downstream transaction flow to support legitimate professional services.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 using the Gibraltar bank's London correspondent clearing arrangements. The payment reference should state 'Capital Contribution' or 'Share Subscription' with the unique company reference, and the bank will require the signed board resolution, updated capital schedule, and source-of-funds evidence. Funds in GBP may alternatively be transmitted via CHAPS or FPS at the UK clearing level; amounts above EUR 100,000 are subject to enhanced source-of-funds verification and, where necessary, GFSC confirmation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for AEO audit subcontractors, security consultants, and certification bodies are cleared through the Gibraltar bank's SWIFT MT103 single-payment channel; batch payroll or recurring audit-fee payments use the bank's multi-payment file. For larger procurement of surveillance systems or travel-related trade services, a commercial letter of credit opened on SWIFT MT700/MT710 is accepted, together with the underlying invoice, audit contract, and customs/export documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward FX contract (GIP/GBP, GIP/EUR, GIP/USD)
